questions.text: With earlier key/value projections cached, what must still happen for the newly processed token during decode?

options.A: Every earlier token must have its key/value projections recomputed.
options.B: The model can skip predicting a next-token distribution entirely.
options.C: Its query attends to cached keys/values before predicting the next token.
options.D: All model weights are replaced by the cached key/value vectors.

questions.explanation: KV caching reuses old projections. Computation for the new token, attention over available context, and next-token prediction still occur.

questions.text: Two batch slots are occupied. One request finishes after step 2; the other needs eight more steps. Under continuous batching, what should happen to a waiting request if capacity permits?

options.A: It must wait until the longer request finishes.
options.B: It replaces the longer request and discards that request's output.
options.C: It starts only after both existing KV caches are erased.
options.D: It can enter the freed slot at the next scheduling iteration.

questions.explanation: Continuous batching reuses a completed request's slot without waiting for other active requests to finish, subject to resource and scheduling constraints.

questions.text: KVCache preallocates arrays to max_seq_len. memory_bytes returns their nbytes; used_bytes is proportional to seq_len. Below capacity, what changes after advance(1)?

options.A: Used bytes increase; allocated memory_bytes stays unchanged.
options.B: Allocated memory_bytes increases; used bytes stay unchanged.
options.C: Both allocated and used bytes become zero.
options.D: Neither changes because advance never changes seq_len.

questions.explanation: advance increments seq_len, increasing logical usage. It does not resize the already allocated arrays, so their nbytes remains constant.

source_notes: These questions distinguish avoided old projections from remaining decode computation, continuous slot reuse, and logical cache usage versus allocated arrays.
The implementation is a toy simulation and does not measure production GPU throughput.
